My roleTechnical approachResultDemonstration & evidence

The problem

Existing customer applications need maintenance as well as new features. Changes must fit the surrounding code and avoid disrupting existing behaviour.

My role

During internships and paid development work at Xeropex, I handled tickets, investigated bugs and implemented customer requests in existing applications.

Technical approach

I worked with Git branches, debugging, unit tests and code reviews before changes were merged and released. Understanding the existing code was part of the work, rather than replacing it with a new implementation.

Challenges & decisions

In one case, a price filter could enter an infinite loop under certain conditions and freeze the browser. I worked on a fix that placed boundaries on the input or processing. The lesson was to check edge cases and termination conditions, not only the expected input.

Result

This work gave me practical experience maintaining shared code, responding to feedback and contributing changes within a development team.

How the pieces connect

  1. Ticket / customer request
  2. Investigate existing code
  3. Implement & test
  4. Review & merge

Simplified conceptual workflow. Not an exact internal architecture.

Demonstration & evidence

Customer code remains private. This case describes my responsibilities and a debugging example without publishing confidential implementation details.
